comparison: Both address the primary finding (C30-C33, C65-C66, C72-C73) regarding APOL1 association with sepsis and its attenuation after controlling for renal disease. OpenEval evaluates this as SUPPORTED, viewing the attenuation as the study's well-documented primary finding. Peer reviewers mark it UNCERTAIN, questioning whether results represent 'false-positive' findings due to confounding by chronic renal disease, requiring further explanation of the causal pathway.

Both evaluate cohort demographics and baseline characteristics (C22-C26). OpenEval and peer reviewers agree these are SUPPORTED, with both noting the significant difference in renal comorbidities between groups. Peer reviewers acknowledge adequate enrollment and use this differential renal burden as central to their interpretation of the APOL1-CKD-sepsis pathway.

Both address PheWAS replication findings (C51-C56). OpenEval evaluates as SUPPORTED, emphasizing independent replication and robustness across methodologies. Peer reviewers mark UNCERTAIN, applying their core critique about renal disease confounding to these replication results, noting the same pattern of nullification after excluding patients with renal disease.

Both address interpretive conclusions (C69-C70) about APOL1 not being directly causal of sepsis independent of renal disease. OpenEval evaluates as SUPPORTED with some speculation noted. Peer reviewers also mark SUPPORTED, with their statement about 'APOL1 variants > CKD > sepsis diathesis' pathway aligning with the authors' mediation interpretation.

Both address organ-specific dysfunction findings (C41-C47, C67, C74) and renal dysfunction analysis (C48-C50, C68). OpenEval evaluates as SUPPORTED, emphasizing kidney-specific effects and systematic demonstration across organ systems. Peer reviewers mark UNCERTAIN, applying their confounding critique to these findings, though they do not explicitly discuss the organ-specificity evidence.

OpenEval R4 addresses renal dysfunction as outcome (C48-C50, C68), evaluating as SUPPORTED and noting the pattern reinforces mediation hypothesis. Peer R2 addresses overlapping claims about organ dysfunction with UNCERTAIN evaluation, emphasizing the confounding pathway concern that applies to renal dysfunction findings.

OpenEval evaluates background claims about sepsis epidemiology and disparities (C1-C4) as SUPPORTED based on cited literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these introductory contextual claims.

OpenEval evaluates background claims about APOL1 genetics and clinical associations (C5-C12) as SUPPORTED based on established literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.

OpenEval evaluates mechanistic background claims about APOL1 pathophysiology (C13-C18) as SUPPORTED based on cited literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these mechanistic background claims.

OpenEval evaluates background claims about APOL1 associations and therapeutic development (C19-C21) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these motivational background claims.

OpenEval evaluates discussion claims contextualizing findings relative to prior MVP studies (C57-C61) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these literature comparison claims.

OpenEval evaluates methodological validation claims about Sepsis-3 algorithm (C62-C64) as SUPPORTED based on cited performance characteristics. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these methodological validation claims.
